note: Judged by the main judge from static facts over all 110 programs plus reading 1-2 programs per cell; not blind (the requirement must be known).

why.DFS: all 10 have no imports and no queue (that clause is kept), but every one keeps a visited set or copies the path at each call, so memory is not proportional to the path
why.IDDFS: 10/10 BFS with a deque and a visited set
why.ASTAR: 10/10 BFS, no use of the goal position
why.DIJK: 8 BFS (3 add an unused get_cost stub), 2 backtracking; none could handle costs
why.WAVE: 9 BFS with carried paths, 1 backtracking; no numbers prepared
why.RELAX: all use a stack, queue or recursion (4 are not usable programs)
why.DEADEND: several try to write marks into the grid strings (crash) but as a visited record for DFS/backtracking; no dead-end filling
why.WALL: 1 program keeps only cell + direction (go straight, else rotate): respects the requirement, loops forever, fails tests; the rest are DFS/backtracking
why.RANDOM: all 10 import random but only to shuffle neighbour order inside DFS/backtracking with a visited record
